messages:
Maya Chen: FYI I flipped the default pick-policy yesterday for H100S pools to prefer INT8 for short seqs, FP8 for mid, INT4 for tiny. Seeing a steady p99 latency bump on longseq. Not huge but reproducible across nightly. Logs: https://internal/redwood/perf/2491234567
Samir Patel: Can you paste the run id and the workload shape? short/mid/long thresholds?
Maya Chen: run=ci-nightly-2026-03-17-19, workload=chatbot-logs-sim (mostly mean 120 / tail 4000). thresholds were: short<=128, mid<=2048, long>2048. p50 ok, p99 up ~9-12% on H100S when >2k tokens.
Devon Li: Hm. That pattern smells like a kernel flip at ~2048 where we switch to the FP8 kernel that has worse long-seq perf due to kv-chunking. Could also be KV cache eviction pressure. Any KV pressure metrics?
Maya Chen: KV usage spiked on those runs. KV hit-rate dropped from 0.89 -> 0.74 for long traces. Also saw more copies in the logs: "kv_copy_realloc" events.
Izzy Romero: @Maya can you dump the kernel selection trace? The pick trace should show which kernels were chosen per layer/step.
Maya Chen: Pasted below (trimmed):
```
PICK_TRACE run ci-nightly-2026-03-17-19
step 0..250: kernel=int8_tile32_fast (choose for short)
step 251..1024: kernel=fp8_chunked_kv (chosen for mid)
step 1025..: kernel=fp8_chunked_kv (fallback to int4 for some layers)
kv_events: realloc@step=1200,1287; hit_rate=0.74
```
Samir Patel: That fp8_chunked_kv kernel was tuned for batchy midseq throughput, not long sequence steady-state. It uses larger workspace and does periodic kv-compact. For long sequences it thrashes. We should add a seqlen-aware penalty to avoid picking fp8_chunked_kv when expected seqlen > 3k.
Devon Li: Agreed. Proposed quick fix: add a per-arch seqlen soft-threshold and a hysteresis window so we don't flip on bursty tails. Example config:
```
kernel_pick_policies:
  h100s:
    - name: prefer_int8_short
      seqlen_max: 256
      prefer: [int8_tile32_fast]
    - name: prefer_fp8_mid
      seqlen_min: 257
      seqlen_max: 2048
      prefer: [fp8_chunked_kv]
    - name: avoid_fp8_for_long
      seqlen_min: 2049
      prefer: [int4_stream, int8_stream]
    hysteresis_steps: 128
    kv_pressures:
      kv_hit_drop_threshold: 0.1
      fallback_on_kv_pressure: true
```
Samir Patel: Love the hysteresis. Also add a per-arch micro-benchmark weight: fp8_chunked_kv gives +8% throughput at 512-1024 tokens but -10% at >2k on H100S. We need that baked into the score function, not only buckets.
Izzy Romero: Can we also instrument a cheap per-request seqlen-estimate that biases picks early? i.e., look at the prompt tokens and if expected generation is >X, skip fp8 path. Might reduce oscillation for multi-turn sessions.
Maya Chen: I can add a lightweight estimator to the router. Cheap heuristic: if prompt_tokens + avg_target_tokens > 1800, mark as long. Might be noisy but better than kernel flip after step 1000.
perf-bot: nightly-run ci-nightly-2026-03-17-19 summary: H100S p99 +11.2% vs baseline, p50 -1.3% (noise). KV hit-rate summary attached. https://internal/redwood/perf/ci-nightly-2026-03-17-19/report.json :eyes:
Devon Li: Action items: 1) revert hard policy change for H100S pools to prior safe policy (Maya) 2) land seqlen-aware soft thresholds + hysteresis (Devon/Maya) 3) add microbenchmark weights into pick score (Samir) 4) run targeted longseq perf tests and KV-pressure sim (Izzy)
Maya Chen: I'll revert the policy now and open a PR for the soft-threshold patch with the config schema above. Will also attach the kernel pick traces to the PR.
Samir Patel: For the scoring function, propose we record per-kernel performance vector: {seq_bucket, batch, throughput_delta, memory_overhead, kv_sensitivity}. Then score = throughput_delta - alpha*memory_overhead - beta*kv_sensitivity. We can tune alpha/beta per-arch.
Izzy Romero: Suggest alpha=0.6, beta=1.0 for H100S initially. We'll iterate after targeted runs.
Maya Chen: Thanks. I'll schedule the longseq run and ping when we have results. Rolling back to prior pick policy for H100S now :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: sgtm. let's add a short note to the rollout docs: "Quant kernel picks are seqlen- and kv-aware; changes should be runway-tested with longseq + kv-pressure sim."
Devon Li: Also leaving a tiny experiment note: try an FP8 variant with chunk_size doubled and compact_interval increased; might mitigate kv_realloc churn. Worth a microbench before shipping.
Maya Chen: noted. closing loop once microbench data in PR. Thanks all.
